title: UNIT 1: PHYSICS AND HUMAN SOCIETY
notes:
✓ Physics → Studies matter, energy, motion, forces and their interactions.

✓ It provides the knowledge needed to understand nature, develop technology, solve practical problems and improve society.

notes:

Encourage interest in physics.

Disseminate scientific knowledge.

◆ EPS OBJECTIVES

title: 1.3 MAKING OF PHYSICS KNOWLEDGE
notes:
✓ Physics knowledge → Is developed through observation, reasoning, experimentation, evidence, measurement, analysis and communication.

◆ SOURCES OF KNOWLEDGE

◆ EXPERIENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
✓ Knowledge obtained through direct experience.

✓ Sensory perception → Information through seeing, touching, hearing, etc.

✓ Introspection → Examining one's own thoughts and feelings.

✓ Memory → Retaining and recalling experiences.

✓ Testimony → Information obtained from spoken or written sources.

◆ NON-EXPERIENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
✓ Knowledge obtained through reasoning, logic, mathematics and existing knowledge without direct personal experience.

◆ SCIENTIFIC METHOD
✓ Observation → Question/Problem → Hypothesis → Experiment → Data Collection → Analysis → Conclusion → Communication.

◆ EXAMPLE
✓ To investigate altitude and water's boiling point:
Change altitude → Measure boiling temperature → Record data → Analyze relationship → Draw conclusion.

✓ Generally, the boiling point of water decreases as altitude increases because atmospheric pressure decreases.

◆ SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE
✓ Evidence-based • Testable • Reproducible • Open to revision when reliable new evidence is obtained.

title: 1.4 MISSION OF PHYSICS AND CAREER AWARENESS
notes:
✓ Physics → Advances scientific knowledge, engineering and innovation for the benefit of society.

◆ MISSION OF PHYSICS
Understand laws and principles of nature.
Advance science and engineering.
Develop scientific thinking and problem-solving.
Support technological innovation.
Apply knowledge to societal problems.

◆ PHYSICS CAREERS

◆ HEALTHCARE → Medical physicist • Radiation specialist • Medical imaging • Radiotherapy.

◆ ENGINEERING → Engineering physics • Electronics • Mechanical systems • Manufacturing.

◆ ENERGY → Renewable energy • Nuclear energy • Solar/wind systems • Energy research.

◆ TECHNOLOGY → Electronics • Computing • Telecommunications • Instrumentation.

◆ GEOPHYSICS & METEOROLOGY → Earth science • Weather • Climate • Atmospheric physics • Environmental research.

◆ RESEARCH & DATA → Research scientist • Data scientist • Laboratory research • Scientific computing.

✓ Key idea → Physics provides analytical, mathematical, experimental and problem-solving skills for many careers.

title: PHYSICS AND OTHER FIELDS
notes:
✓ Physics → Is interdisciplinary and works together with many fields.

✓ Physics + Biology → Biophysics.
✓ Physics + Medicine → Medical physics.
✓ Physics + Computer Science → Computational physics.
✓ Physics + Astronomy → Astrophysics.
✓ Physics + Chemistry → Physical chemistry.
✓ Physics + Earth science → Geophysics.
✓ Physics + Engineering → Engineering physics and technological applications.
✓ Physics + Mathematics → Mathematical modeling.

✓ Key idea → Physics provides fundamental principles used to understand and solve problems across many disciplines.

title: 1.5 CURRENT STATUS OF PHYSICS
notes:
✓ Modern physics → Continues to develop through discoveries, advanced experiments and new technologies.

◆ EXOPLANETS
✓ Planets outside our Solar System.

◆ BLACK HOLES
✓ Extremely dense regions where gravity is so strong that even light cannot escape.

◆ QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY
✓ Uses principles of quantum physics to provide highly secure communication.

◆ HIGH-ENERGY PHYSICS
✓ Studies fundamental particles and the interactions between them.

◆ GRAVITATIONAL WAVES
✓ Ripples in spacetime produced by violent cosmic events such as merging massive objects.

◆ GLOBAL WARMING
✓ Physics helps explain Earth's climate, radiation, energy transfer and atmospheric processes.

◆ JAMES WEBB SPACE TELESCOPE (JWST)
✓ Advanced space telescope used to study the early universe, galaxies, stars, planetary systems and exoplanets.

◆ HIGGS BOSON
✓ A fundamental particle associated with the Higgs field, which explains how elementary particles acquire mass.

✓ Key idea → Modern physics continues to expand our understanding of the universe while creating new technologies and applications.
